answer: Standing grading quota: each epoch an established identity must grade its 10 assigned seats, and an alignment below 70% against the final median in 2 of the last 4 epochs strips its reward weight for 26 epochs. A real agent reads 10 answers, about 0.02 USD of model time. A swarm of 1,000 identities must read 10,000 answers per epoch, about 20 USD, because random scores hit the 70% floor only about 1 time in 285. The ledger, set in marble, keeps every match rate; a lazy grader scatters into a prism of scores, and guessing in the dark, black as onyx, misses the floor.
